choices.label: B
choices.text: Hematogenous seeding from a breast primary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactive change from a Bartholin abscess

explanation.summary: Inguinal lymphadenopathy in vulvar cancer reflects lymphatic spread in advanced disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vulvar carcinoma usually presents as a unifocal plaque, ulcer or mass, and inguinal lymphadenopathy may be present in advanced disease, reflecting lymphatic spread. This is why inguinal node evaluation is part of management.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoimmune T-cell infiltrates are in the skin of lichen sclerosus, not a cause of firm nodes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Synchronous breast cancer is a concern in Paget disease; regional nodes here reflect the vulvar tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chronic scratching causes lichen simplex chronicus, not lymphoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: There is no fluctuant introital abscess; the ulcerated labial mass is the likely source.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old woman undergoes radical local excision of a vulvar squamous cell carcinoma with inguinal lymph node evaluation. Pathology shows tumor at the surgical margin and metastatic carcinoma in two inguinal nodes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

explanation.summary: Positive nodes or inadequate margins after vulvar cancer surgery call for adjuvant radiation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adjuvant radiation may be used after surgery for vulvar cancer with high-risk findings such as involved lymph nodes or inadequate surgical margins. Chemoradiation as primary therapy is reserved for locally advanced disease that cannot be managed surgically.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Topical steroids treat dermatoses and do not address residual or nodal carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Involved nodes and positive margins are high-risk findings that warrant adjuvant treatment, not observation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Evaluation for synchronous carcinomas belongs to the Paget disease workup, not SCC margins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Imiquimod is for noninvasive HPV-associated VIN, not residual invasive cancer.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman has a large, biopsy-proven vulvar squamous cell carcinoma invading adjacent structures. The surgical team determines that the disease cannot be managed surgically. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

explanation.summary: Locally advanced vulvar cancer that cannot be managed surgically is treated with chemoradiation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of vulvar cancer depends on stage. Resectable disease is excised with inguinal node evaluation, whereas locally advanced disease that cannot be managed surgically is treated with chemoradiation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Steroids and surveillance are lichen sclerosus management, not cancer treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Laser ablation treats noninvasive HPV-associated VIN, not invasive carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Marsupialization treats recurrent Bartholin cysts or abscesses.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Imiquimod is for HPV-associated VIN when invasion is not suspected.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman has several raised vulvar lesions. Biopsy shows HPV-associated vulvar high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion, and nothing suggests invasive cancer. She strongly prefers to avoid an operation. Which of the following is an appropriate treatment?

explanation.summary: Topical imiquimod is a nonsurgical option for HPV-associated VIN when invasion is not suspected.
explanation.whyCorrect: HPV-associated VIN (vulvar HSIL) may be treated with surgical excision, laser ablation, or topical imiquimod when invasive cancer is not suspected. Differentiated VIN, by contrast, is treated with surgical excision.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adjuvant radiation follows cancer surgery with positive nodes or margins; this is a noninvasive lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Marsupialization treats recurrent Bartholin cysts or abscesses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clobetasol treats lichen sclerosus and LSC, not an HPV-related precursor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tacrolimus is a second-line treatment for lichen sclerosus.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old woman has a pruritic, erythematous, eczema-like vulvar plaque that has not improved with emollients. Biopsy shows large pale cells within the squamous epithelium; special stains show that these cells contain mucin. Which of the following best classifies this lesion?

explanation.summary: Extramammary Paget disease is an intraepithelial adenocarcinoma of mucin-secreting Paget cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is extramammary Paget disease, a rare intraepithelial adenocarcinoma of postmenopausal women. Its Paget cells are mucin-secreting adenocarcinoma cells within the squamous epithelium; invasive adenocarcinoma may be present within or beneath the surface lesion in up to 25% of patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lichen sclerosus is the autoimmune dermatosis; it shows dermal homogenization, not intraepithelial glandular cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Classic VIN is an HPV-driven squamous precursor made of basaloid, not mucin-secreting, cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Keratinizing SCC forms invasive nests with keratin pearls, not mucin-containing intraepithelial cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lichen simplex chronicus is reactive thickening from scratching, without neoplastic cells.
